gen-dafont-junegull-gf-khula: Chunky, pinched, a little retro: Junegull squeezes its curves nearly shut and stands tall. Khula takes the opposite line, tall in the middle with mouths held open, so the heading's tight shapes get room to breathe beside it.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-krub: Retro and friendly, with pinched curve openings and none of the thick-thin flicker that catches the eye. Junegull is built to be seen, while Krub, its x-height pronounced and its loops left unfinished, is built to be read.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-kufam: Junegull has a retro, friendly build, pinching the mouth of every curve and skipping any thick-thin flicker. But Kufam, drawn like a neon tube with generous e curves, can take a slightly larger size.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-lexend: Friendly and retro, Junegull pinches its curves while holding a lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals. Lexend supplies the real draw: outsized lowercase and open jaws on every curve, a clear counterpoint to the closed heading.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-lexend-deca: No thick-thin flicker anywhere in Junegull, just pinched curves and a lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals. Junegull makes the statement; Lexend Deca does the unshaded, open-curved reading.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-liter: Liter reads with no stroke contrast at all, its lowercase standing tall and its round forms wide-mouthed. And Junegull earns its keep big and brief, where its pinched curves and cast-iron stature can show.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-mada: Mada reads approachable and modern, its curves refusing to close and its towering midzone filling every line it sets. Junegull, retro and pinched, gives that openness a snug, friendly foil.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-martel-sans: Martel Sans reads neutral and modern, with generous openings in every curve and a high mean line across each word. Junegull handles the retro statement; Martel Sans handles the rest.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-matangi: Junegull is retro, friendly, and pinched at every curve. Matangi, with twine-like strokes, rounded letters left open and a hefty lowercase, should read in a warm, easygoing way line after line.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-maven-pro: Maven Pro keeps its lines gentle and uniform, high-waisted, with a welcoming gap in the c. Maven Pro blown up starts to compete with Junegull, whose pinched curves lose their punch if the heading shrinks.
